semantic_checklist.reasoning: Finiteness characterizes class membership, but it does not preserve the source's full exact numerical norm prescription, especially the printed K3/property-3 clause.

semantic_checklist.reasoning: The reconstruction consistently follows display (2.21), but therefore does not encode the other non-definitionally-identical operator/parameter prescription that is also literally printed in the immutable source.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source purports to identify the numerical psi_1 norm, not merely whether some admissible norm scale is finite.

semantic_checklist.reasoning: An exact value definition entails the corresponding finiteness characterization, but the finiteness characterization cannot recover the exact value; the reconstructed relation is strictly weaker.

translation_implies_source.reasoning: The reconstruction implies the display-based finiteness characterization, but it cannot imply the source's full exact norm definition or its literal claim that the norm is the smallest K3 in property 3. Finiteness alone does not determine a numerical norm. For a constant X = a > 0, the least K3 for property (c) is a, while the display-(2.21) infimum is a/log(2), so the omitted distinction is genuine rather than definitional.

source_implies_translation.reasoning: The source's property-(a)--(d) equivalence implies that one property has a finite positive scale exactly when property (d) has one; display (2.21) identifies the latter scales with the admissible one-point set. Thus the selected source context entails the reconstructed finiteness equivalence. This implication remains valid whether the disputed norm prose is read literally as property (c) or corrected by the following display, because only existence/finiteness, not equality of the optimal constants, is needed.

findings.source_evidence: Definition 2.7.5 literally says 'smallest K3 in property 3,' but Proposition 2.7.1(c) is an interval exponential-moment condition and display (2.21) is the one-point condition associated with property (d) and K4.
findings.translation_evidence: The reconstructed infimum uses only the one-point exponential condition with threshold 2 and treats the interval condition as a separate alternative.
findings.impact: The reconstruction chooses the displayed K4-shaped formula and cannot be equivalent to both consecutive printed norm descriptions; the immutable source defect requires an explicit adjudication/corpus-policy decision.

findings.source_evidence: The source assigns an exact numerical psi_1 norm via a smallest-constant/infimum definition.
findings.translation_evidence: The reconstructed proposition asserts only that the one-point infimum is below infinity exactly when one of four conditions has a witness.
findings.impact: The formal proposition preserves sub-exponential class membership but not the complete quantitative norm definition, so it is source-implied but does not imply the whole selected definition.

findings.source_evidence: The source binder is a random variable.
findings.translation_evidence: The reconstructed outer binder permits arbitrary real functions but places measurability inside every scale and property.
findings.impact: Nonmeasurable functions make both sides false before the equivalence is formed; this adds no substantive counterexample on the source domain.

rationale: The round trip faithfully reconstructs the display-(2.21) one-point scale, all four qualitative sub-exponential conditions, the absence of centering, and their finiteness/class-membership equivalence. It is nevertheless weaker than the selected Definition 2.7.5 because it asserts only finiteness and does not preserve the exact norm assignment, most importantly the immutable conflict between the literal K3/property-3 prose and the following K4-shaped one-point display. The robust implication pair is translation-to-source no and source-to-translation yes, hence not-faithful-weaker and not accepted. Adjudication is requested to record which printed branch governs the benchmark and how this known source defect is counted; it must not be silently corrected.
